slice_id: F5a / Packet 8 / durable ChainLedger-backed consume-once admission gate (closes F5A-R23)
adr: ADR-0147 - durable ChainLedger-backed consume-once admission gate (Packet 8, closes F5A-R23)
task: DESIGN-ONLY packet: propose the ADR for Packet 8, durable consume-once, which closes F5A-R23. No production code, pipeline code, or test file was written or edited. No RED/GREEN. No merge.
proposal: Replaces the publicly-reachable _spend constructor-kwdefault tuple in HistoricalStudyVerifier.capture (dskit/production/verifier.py:834, type(self).__init__.__kwdefaults__['_spend'][:2]) with a durable, ChainLedger/JsonlLedger-backed consume-once gate, per the owner-approved store (evidence 0100) and the owner-approved migration/issuer decisions (evidence 0144). Builds on, rather than re-derives, the same-session prior design chain (evidence 0138 design+matrix, 0139 review: 4 Major, 0140 corrections, 0141 handoff review: 4 Major still open, 0142 final clarifications) which was left with owner gates P8-D1-M1 (sequencing/migration) and P8-D1-M4 (bootstrap/namespace provisioning) open; 0144 closed both at the owner level on 2026-09-15 but kept implementation blocked until Packets 5-7 closed. P7 closed 2026-09-17 (RE-ENTRY.md current checkpoint), so this ADR is the first document able to act on 0144's approval. Two corrections were found reading the current code directly for this proposal rather than trusting 0138/0140's prose: (1) ChainLedger has no in-process thread lock today (grep confirms only the cross-process serve.lock flock exists), so the 'single RLock' 0140 describes is new surface this ADR must add, stated explicitly rather than assumed pre-existing; (2) admission_ref's validated shape, read directly from trust.py's _p4_reference_bytes (trust.py:2275-2306), is exactly {kind, role, schema, sha256}, all str, role fixed 'study-lifecycle', confirming 0140's 'four-field IssuanceBasisRef.v1' description precisely rather than by name only. The adopted design: a new read-only inspect_capture_admission accessor on the existing issued CapturedAuthorizationAuthority (trust.py, dispatched through the existing closed type(resolver) if/elif/else pattern, no new production import); an idempotency key 'admission_use:v1:' + canonical_hash({kind, schema, sha256}) of the verified admission_ref, deliberately excluding process/run/nonce identity; a new admission_use record kind (schema dskit.admission-use/v1, body {schema, admission_ref, binding_sha256}) added to vocab.py RECORD_KINDS and state.py's _FOLDS fold table; a new ChainLedger.reserve_once(record) -> (created: bool, seq: int) atomic API plus a new self._transition_lock (RLock) covering reserve_once/append/append_many/barrier/snapshot/close; five health states (opening/healthy/uncertain/closed/readonly) gating every mutating call; a capture order that reserves-then-barriers before any delegate call, with only the (True, seq) caller ever invoking authority.capture, and no unspend/rollback/retry after a durable reservation; a new HistoricalStudyVerifier.durable(authority, root, *, clock) classmethod that constructs its OWN ServeRoot/JsonlLedger from an owner-configured directory and a fixed private series-id constant, never accepting a caller-built Ledger instance (closing 0139's P8-D1-M4 bare-ledger-injection replay bypass); and a full-replay (not partial-fold-trust) recovery contract after any uncertain-state failure, addressing 0141's P8-D1-M5. bind()'s admission artifact is retired; _REQUIRED_PLAN narrows from six names to the five ADR-0125 plan artifacts (scope_intent, ces, pea, bvp, cas), unchanged by this ADR. authorize_capture_set (the separate, already-ledger-backed P4 batch route, ADR-0143/0144) is confirmed untouched by direct inspection -- it never reads _spend or _admission_spent.
scope: Design proposal only: ADR-0147 appended to docs/architecture/decision-log.md and this evidence file. No dskit/ production code, pipeline code, or test file was written or edited. No RED/GREEN. No merge.
non_goals: Editing or weakening authorize_capture_set, commit_p4_batch, _p4_close_admission, _dynamic_p4_close_admission, or any ADR-0143/0144 dynamic-dispatch code. A second writer, planner, ledger or tape engine. Claiming OS-owned external-broker deployment durability, multi-machine replication, or any guarantee beyond the same-filesystem process-restart boundary. Real data, replay, HPO/refit, backtest, paper/live activity or deployment of any kind. Whole-F5a closure or unblocking F3/F5b. Wiring HistoricalStudyVerifier.durable(...) into compose.py's live serving bundle. Any change to bind()'s five retained plan artifacts or ADR-0125's private-plan-precedes-capture ordering. Any change to JsonlLedger's five store hooks, rotation, durability grading, or libs/sqlite.py's parallel store beyond the shared ChainLedger base gaining reserve_once/_transition_lock once and inheriting.

open_question_for_reviewer: Decision point 9's HistoricalStudyVerifier.durable(authority, root, *, clock) classmethod authenticates the durable namespace only via a fixed private series-id constant plus owner-configured directory trust (root is never caller/admission-derived) -- it does not add any stronger binding between the issued P4 authority instance and the ChainLedger instance beyond both being supplied by the same trusted composition call. Should Phase 0 additionally require the durable factory to record and check some authority-identifying value (e.g. a stable authority/broker id) inside the admission_use body, so that two DIFFERENT authority instances reusing the same root/series cannot each reserve against admissions the other never actually verified -- or is that already excluded by construction, since only an issued, non-revoked authority ever produces a verifiable admission_ref via inspect_capture_admission in the first place?

preapproval_review.summary: An independent preapproval review of the prior revision of this ADR draft found 1 Major and 2 Minor and 2 Nit findings. The reviewer confirmed the 2 Minors and 2 Nits as legitimately deferred, non-blocking -- their content is not reproduced here pending the reviewer's own written record; only the 1 Major required a correction to this draft.
preapproval_review.major_finding: Cross-process reserve_once atomicity was asserted in Decision point 6 and Decision point 11's 'Second-process contention' bullet without citing code proving it, or confirming the lock is held for reserve_once's full read-check-then-write duration. Reviewer's own words: "For JsonlLedger, the existing _commit uses fcntl.flock(serve.lock), but the ADR asserts this without citing code or confirming the lock is held during reserve_once's entire _prepare + _commit + barrier sequence... Code inspection of JsonlLedger._open and _commit required to prove this, which the design prose does not provide."
preapproval_review.correction_applied: Decision point 6 now cites the exact lines: _lock_fd's serve.lock flock (fcntl.flock(fd, fcntl.LOCK_EX | fcntl.LOCK_NB), ledger.py:972) is acquired once in __init__ before _open() ever runs (ledger.py:949-956) and released only in close() (ledger.py:980-988, called from close() at ledger.py:1033-1048) -- held continuously for the entire lifetime of a writing ChainLedger/JsonlLedger instance, never released or reacquired around any individual operation. reserve_once's read step (ledger.py:1077, prior = self._index.get(record['id'])) and its append step (ledger.py:1104-1108, _store/_sync/index update) therefore execute inside one unbroken hold of _lock_fd, with no release/reacquire boundary between them for a second process's write to land in. Because _acquire_lock's flock is exclusive and non-blocking (ledger.py:972-977), at most one process can ever hold an open writer on a given series; a second process's constructor fails immediately at _acquire_lock, before _open() or any reserve_once call is reachable, and the identical mechanism (fcntl.flock(LOCK_EX | LOCK_NB) on the same serve.lock path) applies when a caller supplies an externally-held health.InstanceLock instead (health.py:1351-1372). So two processes can never be concurrently inside reserve_once's read-check-append sequence for the same series -- the second cannot even open its writer until the first calls close(), which is strictly after that first process's reserve_once calls have already completed. Decision point 11's 'Second-process contention' bullet was updated to reference this proof instead of restating the unproven assertion. No redesign of Decision point 6's lock strategy was needed (option 2 of the correction task, not 3a/3b): the pre-existing serve.lock flock, once its full acquire/release scope is cited precisely, already covers reserve_once's exact sequence -- nothing new needed to be added to the write path.

recheck.result: 0 Critical, 0 Major, 0 Minor, 0 Nit. READY_FOR_OWNER_APPROVAL: yes.
corrections_verified: independently re-cited ledger.py:949-956 (lock acquired in __init__ before _open), :972 (exclusive non-blocking flock), :980-988/:1033-1048 (released only in close()) -- confirmed only 2 flock call sites in the whole file
independently confirmed reserve_once's read-check (line 1077) through append (1104-1108) executes with no release/reacquire boundary between them, inside the one continuously-held lock

independently confirmed a second process's constructor fails at _acquire_lock (non-blocking) before _open()/reserve_once is ever reachable -- genuine mutual exclusion by construction, not a timing argument
cross-checked the identical mechanism backing health.InstanceLock/_check_held_lock for the externally-supplied-lock path
recheck.new_observation_non_blocking: the design implicitly relies on standard POSIX flock-release-on-process-exit semantics for crash recovery (a crashed writer's lock is released by the OS when its file descriptor closes); this is universally true on the target platforms but not explicitly stated in the ADR text -- recommend adding one sentence during GREEN, not a Phase 0 blocker.
